See User Roles and Permission for more information. For the step by step process on setting up the Announcement-Only Extension kindly go to Article number 4492 in our success site or click the link Announcement-Only Extension - Overview | RingCentral Step 1: The Administrator should log in to the RingCentral Online account then go to the Phone System section on the Admin Portal then click Groups() Others() to open the Groups section then Click on the Others lastly the Announcement only extension in order to modify the Announcement extension settings (see image below). Step 2: Click Announcement > Greeting. Step 3: A pop-up will appear displaying the current Announcement Greeting. Customer have an option wether to use the default or customize an announcement. fields.name: RECORDCOMPANYGREETINGSWALKTHROUGH
fields.fieldText:
RECORD COMPANY GREETINGS WALKTHROUGH The Company Greeting and Menu section provides additional call handling options, including hearing the Default greeting and recording a Custom greeting. This is a great way to specify the greeting callers will hear when they call the main company number, during Company or Business Hours, and After Hours. NOTE: To set up Company Call Handling Rules, go to Setting your Company Call Handling and Operator Extension. Clicking on Advanced will allow you to Set Up Advanced Company Call Handling rules via the Auto-Receptionist.. For the step by step process on setting up the company greeting via Auto Receptionist kindly go to Article number 3381 in our success site or click the link Company Greeting - Setup Custom Greeting | RingCentral See instructions below for the brief example of setting up an account's company greeting. Accessing the Company Greeting and Menu Section Step 1: Log in as the Account Administrator in the RingCentral account. Step 2: Go to Admin Portal, and then click Phone System.
Step 3: Click Auto-Receptionist.
Step 4: Click IVR Settings
Default Company Greetings Step 1: Select either Company Hours or After Hours. Click Edit.
Step 2: Select Default on the drop down menu under Set Greeting
Press the play button to hear the sample of the default greeting.
Setting Up Custom Company Greetings for User Hours or After Hours Step 1: Choose between Company Hours or After Hours, and then click Edit.
Step 3: Select Custom to record or upload a personalized greeting for the company. There are three (3) ways to customize the company greeting:
  • Record over the Phone
  • Record over tthe computer microphone
  • Import
Setting the Rule if the Callers Enter No Action Once done setting up the Company Hours and After Hours greeting, the Caller enters no action needs to be set.
  • Connect to Operator
    • Select this option to direct the callers to ext 0, or the Operator Extension, afer the greeting.
  • NOTE: Connect to Operator is selected by Default.
  • Disconnect
    • Select this option to disconnect the caller after the greeting repeat three times.
NOTE: The Operator Extension is an extension that is set up to recieve all calls and messages that comes in the main company number. Customer can assign a User or Call Queue as the Operator Extension. for more information regarding setting up Operator Extension click the link Company Call Handling and Operator Extension - Set up | RingCentral

fields.name: RECORDGREETINGSFORMESSAGEONLYEXTENSION
fields.fieldText:
RECORD GREETINGS FOR MESSAGE ONLY EXTENSION IMPORTANT: Only Super Admins, User Admins, Users with Billing Admin access and the user who can access the extension can view and make changes to this section. See User Roles and Permission for more information. Editing the Messages-Only Extension Name NOTE: Customer's have an option to modify the name of their Annoucement Only Extension, Changing the Name of the extension will affect the name pronounce on the voicemail greeting when the extension is called. this occurs when the Voicemail greeting is set to default. Step 1: Under Groups > Others, select the Message-Only Extension Step 2: Click Extension Info > Record Extension Name Step 3: A pop-up will appear displaying the current Record Extension Name. Customer have an option wether to use the RingCentral text-to-speech name or Record extension name.
  • RingCentral text-to-speech name (RingCentral will pronounce the name based on what is typed on the optional field)
  • Record extension name (Customer have three option to record their custom Message Only Extension name Phone, Record Using Computer Microphone, Import)
Editing the Messages-Only Extension Voicemail Greeting Step 1: On the Messages & Notifications tab you will see the settings that the customer can configure. Voicemail Greeting A pop-up will appear displaying the current Voicemail Greeting. Choose the preffered type of greeting.
  • Default (Changing the message only extension name see above instructions Editing the Messages-Only Extension Name will take effect here when Voicemail Greeting is set to default)
  • Custom (Selecting this option will allow the customer to record a custom voicemail greeting in three ways
    • Record Over the Phone
    • Record Using Computer Microphone
    • Import
For the step by step process on setting up Message only Extension, kindly go to Article number 4491 in our success site or click the link Message-Only Extension - Overview | RingCentral

fields.name: RECORDNAME
fields.fieldText:
RECORD NAME Admin: Record another User's Name RingCentral reads the First and Last Name saved in an extension's User Details as part of the default User Greeting or Voicemail Greeting. This can be customized with the help of the Record User Name option which can be found on the General tab in the User Details section. This option ensures that a User's name is correctly pronounced by the system. Use RingCentral text-to-speech to create a phonetic spelling of the User's name so the system can pronounce it correctly and be used for announcements. Use Record my name to create a recording by following the prompts on the phone, or by recording it straight from your computer microphone, or by uploading a .wav or .mp3 file. NOTE: Recommended audio formats include the following:
  • CCITT u-Law (G711a), 8kHz, 8 bit, mono
  • PCM, 8kHz, 16 bit, mono
NOTE: Administrators should log in to the RingCentral Online accoint then go to My Extension in order to modify his own extension's settings. Check User Details - Record your User Name | RingCentral for directions. IMPORTANT: Only Super Admins, User Admins, and Users with Billing Admin access can view and make changes to this section. See User Roles and Permissions | RingCentral for more information. For the step by step process on setting up User Name via Administrator kindly go to Article number 1763 in our success site or click the link User Settings - Admin - Record User's user name See instructions below for the brief walkthrough. The Administrator should log in to the RingCentral Online account then go to the Users section on the Admin Portal in order to modify the Users' setings. Customizing another extensions's User Name Step 1: On the User list > Users With Extensions tab, click the User's name. Step 2: Click User Details. Step 3: On the General tab, clik Edit below Record User Name. At this point the Customer have two options for recording the Name of the extension
  • RingCentral text-to-speech (RingCentral will pronounce the name based on what is typed on the Greeting Name field)
  • Record My Name
    • By clicking the red small icon the customer will have three option to record either by Phone, Computer, Import.
USER: Record your User Name For the step by step process on setting up the Name via User extersion kindly go to Article number 9722 in our success site or click the link User Details - Record your User Name | RingCentral Setting Up a Call Queue group Name IMPORTANT: Only Super Admins, User Admins, and Users with Billing Admin access can view and make changes to this section. See User Roles and Permissions | RingCentral for more information. Step 1: The Administrator should log in to the RingCentral Online account then go to the Phone System section on the Admin Portal then click Groups() Others() to open the Groups section then Click on the Call Queue lastly the Call Queue extension in order to modify the Call Queue extension settings (see image below). Step 2: Under the Info section of the Call Queue Extension, Click the Record At this point the Customer have two options for recording the Name of the call queue extension
  • Custom (by clicking on the red circle icon the customer have three option in recording a custom Call queue name Record over the phone, Record over computer microphone, Import)
  • RingCentral text-to-speech name (RingCentral will pronounce the name based on what is typed on the optional field)

fields.name: RECORDUSERORGROUPGREETING
fields.fieldText:
RECORD USER OR GROUP GREETING Admin: Setup an extension's User Greeting RingCentral system comes with a default personal greeting, such as "Thank you for calling (user name)." Custom greetings allow the customer to change what their callers hear when they connect to an extension. The User Greeting feature is disabled by default and is not a personal voicemail announcement. Customer can have this option enabled if they prefer the system to answer the call with a recorded welcome message so callers know they have reached the right person. For the step by step process on setting up the user greeting via Auto Receptionist kindly go to Article number 3913 in our success site or click the link User Greeting - Set Up Custom Greeting | Administrators | RingCentral NOTE: Administrator should log in to the RingCentral Online account then go to My Extension in order to configure their User Greeting. Check User: User Settings - Set up User Greeting | RingCentral for instructions. IMPORTANT: Only Super Admins, User Admins, and User Admin access can set up an extension's User Greeting. See User Roles and Permissions | RingCentral for more information. See instructions below for the brief example of setting up a Admin: Setup an extension's User Greeting. Step 1: Administrator should log in to the RingCentral Online account and go to the Users section on the Admin Portal. Step 2: On the User list > <Users With Extensions tab, Click the User. Step 3: Click Screening, Greeting, & Hold Music. Step 4: Click User Hours or After Hours. Step 5: Check Enable below User Greeting, then click Edit. Step 6: Make sure Set Greeting is set to Custom. Step 7: Select how the customer prefer to customize the User Greeting
  • Record over the Phone
  • Record over Computer Microphone
  • Import
User: Set up User Greeting For the step by step process on setting up the user greeting via User: Set up User Greeting kindly go to Article number 9720 in our success site or click the link User Greeting - Set Up Custom Greeting | Administrators | RingCentral Admin: Uploading Custom Greetings for a Call Queue For the step by step process on setting up the custom greeting for a Call Queue group kindly go to Article number 3532 in our success site or click the link Call Queue - Admin: Set Up Custom Greeting | RingCentral

fields.name: RECORDINGBYIMPORTING
fields.fieldText:
RECORDING BY IMPORTING This option will allow the customer to upload a customized pre-recorded audio file stored from their computer/device. Walk the customer through this by following the steps below: Step 1: Click Importing and then, click Browse. Note: After the customer click Browse, they will see a pop-up window where they can locate and select the file that they want to use as their On-demand Call Recording Announcement. They can only use .wav or .mp3 audio files with the following format best audio quality:
  • CCITT u-Law (G711a), 8 kHz, 8-bit, mono
  • PCM, 8 kHz, 16-bit, mono
Step 2:Click Open. Step 3:Click Done. Step 4: Click the Play button to listen to the recording. IMPORTANT: If the quality of the audio is not as clear the sound quality when played on the customer's computer, inform the customer that RingCentral system auto convert their uploaded audio to our supported file indicated below.
  • CCITT u-Law (G711a), 8 kHz, 8-bit, mono
  • PCM, 8 kHz, 16-bit, mono
Note: Background music and HD files will be converted to RingCentral recommended file size and quality this may affect audio quality.

fields.fieldText: Recording successfully imported?

fields.name: RECORDINGBYPHONE
fields.fieldText:
RECORDING BY PHONE This option will allow the customer to record their customized greeting over the phone. Walk the customer through this by following the steps below: Step 1: Ask the customer to enter their phone number on the box provided that RingCentral system can call. Step 2: Whenever they are ready ask the customer to click Call Now. IMPORTANT: Customer's will receive an automated call from RingCentral on the number the they selected, with the instructions for recording their custom greetings. Press 1 to start recording and when they are done, ask them to press the pound # key. After they press the pound # key, the following prompts will be announced:
  • Press 1 - Save your custom greeting.

fields.name: RINGCENTRALGREETINGSSETUP
fields.fieldText:
RINGCENTRAL GREETINGS SET UP This guide will walk you through on how to set up Greetings via online portal. Before proceeding make sure the phone number the customer wants the greeting to play is isolated and if its an extension make sure the extension is activated. The guide covers the following topics below.
  • Company Greeting
    • Calls to customer's company number can be connected to a built-in Auto-Receptionist or connected to a specific extension. When they choose to connect the calls to RingCentral's built-in Auto-Receptionist, the Company Greeting will be played to welcome their callers when they dial the customer's RingCentral Number.
    • Note: Only an account Administrator with access to the Auto-Receptionist will be able to record this greeting. Guide does not include settingg Advance Call Handling setting greetings kindly check Advance Call Handling Option Guide for this information
  • User or Group Greeting
    • Turn on this option when a customer wants the system to answer the call with a recorded welcome message so callers know they've reached the right person or Call Group when they press an extension.
    • Note: Customer's can also use their own User Greeting by adding a Custom Greeting to their User Extension, or customize a Call Group's greeting.
  • User or Group Voicemail Greeting
    • Callers hear this greeting when they are routed to the customer voicemail to leave a message.
    • Note: Customer's can customize User's Voicemail Greeting. as well as a Call Group's Voicemail Greetings.
  • Name
    • Use this option to ensure the Group Name or Extension's Name is pronounced correctly by the system operator. Customer's can spell out the name the way it sounds to help the operator, or they can record the name in customer's own voice and use it for announcements instead.
    • Customer's Extension or Call Group's name is converted with text-to-speech technology.
    • Note: Customers can customize your User Extension's Name or a Group's Name via Online Portal.
  • Announcement
    • Great for when customer's want to provide directions, events information, or any other announcement. Callers will not be given an option to leave messages. This guide is only for Announcement Only Extension Greeting.
    • Note: Walkthrough does not include On-Demand and Automatic Call Recording Announcement, Kindly follow the Call Recording for steps in configuring On-Demand and Automatic Call Recording Announcement.
  • Greeting for Message Only Extension
    • The Message Only Extension also serves as customer's Company's General Mailbox where their callers can leave voice messages. This guide covers customizing the Message Only Extension name, which is pronounce by the system as the name of the extension when the Message Only extension is set to default in the Voice Mail Greeting. Also this guide covers setting up a customized greeting
For more information kindly go to Article 1898 on our success site or click the link Greeting Types | RingCentral

fields.name: TESTOTHERCOMPUTERMICROPHONE
fields.fieldText: TEST OTHER COMPUTER MICROPHONE Ask the customer to plug in the other computer microphone. Before proceeding with recording via Online portal make sure the computer microphone is working by running a test. Walk the customer through in checking if the other microphone is working by following steps below: For Windows Ask the the customer to do the following steps on their computer: Note: By default most Windows Operating System automatically enables microphones and line in ports. 1. Click Start , and then click Control Panel 2. Click Hardware and Sounds, and then click Managing audio devices. A sound window opens. 3. Click the Recording tab. Select the device the customer is using on the selection make sure the icon has a green check mark to make sure that is the default audio input device, if it doesnt have the green checkmark right click the icon then select Enable. 4. To test the microphone, speak into it. 5. After making sure the device is enabled and detected, test if the sound quality of the compupter microphone has no issue by doing a Sound Recorder test. Ask the customer to click Start , All Programs, Accessories, and select Sound Recorder. 6. Click Start Recording (the red circle) and speak into the microphone. 7. When the customer is finish recording, click Stop Recording. A save screen automatically opens. 8. Ask the customer to find and double-click the filename of recording to play back the recorded sound. The file should play from the sound software that is associated with the audio file type - either WAV or WMA. They can open the sound file using Windows Media Player. For MAC Step 1: Click the Apple icon present in the top left corner of the screen. A menu will appear. Step 2: Click System Preferences. Step 3: Under system preferences select Sound either by clicking it or by searching for it in the search text box. Step 4: Under Sound select the Input tab. Step 5: The list of recording devices will appear. Make sure that the “Internal Microphone” is selected if the customer is using a line in port make sure the line in port is selected. Ask the customer to speak into the microphone, and look for blue bars moving beside Input Level while you talk. Note: If the blue bars are rising while the customer is speaking that means the microphone is properly configured skip step 6 - 7 - 8 proceed to step 9, if its not rising proceed to step 6 Step 6: Drag the slider all the way to the right, to set the max volume. Step 7: Now check again if the customer see blue bars rising when they talk into the microphone: if they do, mic is now properly configured. if the blue bars are still not rising proceed to step 8: Step 8: Shut down the machine and then turn it back on Note: After the computer has rebooted follow the steps again and check if the blue bar is rising if its rising proceed to step 9 if its not rising refer the customer to their vendor. Step 9: Ask the customer to open QuickTime Player from Applications folder (if the customer doesnt have the QuickTime Player ask them if they have other recording application installed in the computer. Step 10: Open the File menu and select New Audio Recording. Step 11: The customer will see a very simple user interface with sound recording controls. Ask the customer toclick the Red circle icon to start recording then click the red circle icon again to stop recording. Ask the customer to save the recorded file Step 12. Ask the customer to open the recorded file and press PLAY
